content: New figures show public bodies paid private consultants £3.4bn last year, £1.3bn (62%) more than in 2019-20, and consultant spending remains above pre-pandemic levels. The rise poses a challenge for Keir Starmer’s government, which wants to halve consultant spend this parliament. The Financial Times reported KPMG won a contract worth up to £223m to train civil servants from August; since Labour took office nearly £650m of new consultant contracts have been awarded, many agreed before the transition. Academic and Labour peer Prem Sikka called the reliance on consultants “scandalous,” arguing they contribute little and cannot quickly grasp complex organisations.
